To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) plant size has a positive effect on lean manufacturing practices, whereas unionization and plant size have less pervasive effects on lean practices; (2) four bundles of interrelated lean practices exist and are associated with higher levels of operational performance; and (3) lean bundles are more strongly associated with performance than the practices that compose them.

“the likelihood of implementing lean practices is influenced by plant size, but not unionization or plant age, and the performance of lean plants is strongly associated with their implementation of lean bundles of practices.”

The main takeaway from our work is that

the lean production system is a coherent and internally consistent set of practices that can be implemented as an integrated bundle, and that such a bundle contributes to the operational performance of plants.
lean practices are not implemented in isolation, but rather as part of a coherent set of interrelated practices.

the contextual factors that are most important for lean implementations are plant size and industry, and the contextual factors that have the least influence on lean implementations are age and unionization.
